clue.text: Pump-site (with a capital letter)

parts.note: Paris is the capital city of France
H is simply a letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A pump's location, written with a capital letter, as if giving a spelling instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: The parish pump is the traditional village gathering place for gossip, hence the 'pump-site'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverbial village water pump stood in the local ecclesiastical district, so that district is where the pump sits.

clue.text: Kelvin, in factory, advanced the main food-source

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round

parts.note: a plant is a factory
K is the symbol for kelvin, the temperature unit
on means advanced, as in moved on

explanation.surface: A scientist named Kelvin, working in a factory, developed the staple diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the sea, so this is the sea's food source.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny drifting organisms are the base of the ocean's food chain.

clue.text: They help us to see around Aintree

indicators.note: around means the letters of 'Aintree' are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Binoculars help racegoers see what happens at Aintree, a racecourse near Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National.
explanation.definitionFit: The light-sensitive layers at the back of the eyes enable vision.

clue.text: A flight is contained in this space

definitions.text: A flight is contained in this space

parts.words: A flight is contained in this space
parts.note: a flight of steps runs up the shaft of a building, not an aeroplane in the sky

explanation.definitionFit: The vertical shaft in a building houses the staircase.

clue.text: A good climber, I scale Mt Tumbledown

indicators.note: tumbledown means ramshackle and collapsing, so the letters of 'I scale Mt' fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A mountaineer boasts of conquering a peak called Mount Tumbledown.
explanation.definitionFit: This garden plant is a vigorous vine that scrambles up walls and trellises.

clue.text: Fail to win on points, mind and go mad

parts.note: to lose is to fail to win
taken as written
E and S are compass points, east and south
E and S are compass points, east and south
temper means disposition or frame of mind

explanation.surface: A competitor beaten on points loses control of himself in anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' supplies two compass points, E and S; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To fly into a rage is idiomatically to become angry.

clue.text: Speck of dust found on Tallis's first choral composition

parts.note: a mote is a speck of dust

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of Tallis's

explanation.surface: Dust settles on the first manuscript of a choral work by Tallis, the Tudor composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Tallis was an English Tudor composer of church music; 'found on' links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A polyphonic sacred vocal piece, often unaccompanied.

clue.text: Coated articles can wear out

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: out means the letters of 'wear' are worn out into a new order

explanation.surface: Things with a coating may be worn through.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods made of iron plated with a thin metal layer.

clue.text: Big chief long in the grip of sadomasochism

indicators.note: in the grip of means held inside the other piece

parts.note: S and M, written S&M, abbreviates sadomasochism
to ache is to long for

explanation.surface: A powerful leader secretly yearns for kinky pleasures.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American tribal leader, a paramount chief.

clue.text: Aid to road being put off, it's breaking up naturally

indicators.note: put off means the letters of 'Aid to road being' are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Road-building help is postponed; the road is crumbling of its own accord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is both fodder and part of the indicator phrase in a natural reading; the fodder needs all of AID TO ROAD BEING, so 'put off' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Decay by bacteria and other organisms is decomposition happening by nature.

clue.text: To perform with universal film stars they have to calculate the risks

definitions.text: they have to calculate the risks

parts.note: to act is to perform
U is the British film certificate for a film suitable for everyone
Aries is a constellation and sign of the zodiac, a group of stars

explanation.surface: Actors appearing with film stars are said to be weighing up the dangers.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance companies employ these statisticians to compute probabilities of loss and set premiums.

clue.text: First note from the doctor?

definitions.meaning: the keynote, the first degree of a musical scale
a pick-me-up medicine a doctor might prescribe

explanation.surface: The opening message received from one's GP.
explanation.definitionFit: In music it names the keynote of a scale; in medicine it is a restorative remedy.

clue.text: Family of the sort studied, would you say?

indicators.note: would you say asks the solver to judge the words by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: kind means sort and read means studied, together spoken like the answer

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a family belongs to the type that has been researched.
explanation.walkthrough: KIND (sort) plus READ (studied, said 'red') sounds like the answer; 'of the' is padding linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Relatives by blood form one's kin, the same group as a family.

clue.text: Unconventional silver holder for incense

indicators.note: holder means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: outre is a French borrowing meaning eccentric or unconventional
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An eccentric silver vessel, a censer, for burning incense in church.
explanation.walkthrough: Incense looks like a noun for perfumed smoke, but here it is the verb meaning to anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to make someone furious.

clue.text: Gross orders increased by a quarter

parts.note: OBEs are awards in the Order of the British Empire
E for east, one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: A large purchase order is boosted by twenty-five per cent.
explanation.walkthrough: Gross reads as a bulk total of orders but means very fat; 'increased by' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross can describe a body that is grossly overweight.

clue.text: Tender money to pay for a round!

parts.note: green means young and tender, like new shoots
a fee is money charged

explanation.surface: Offering cash to buy a round of drinks in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: A golf course charges this sum to play a round; the surface suggests buying drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf clubs charge visitors this sum to play a round on the course.

clue.text: Tend to miss Alice, perhaps?

parts.note: to nurse is to tend
a maid is a young unmarried woman, a miss

explanation.surface: Inclined to overlook a girl called Alice.
explanation.walkthrough: In A. A. Milne's poem 'Buckingham Palace', Christopher Robin goes 'down with Alice', his nanny; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice in Milne's poem is a children's nanny, a woman who looks after children.

clue.text: Her lines are no longer valid

definitions.text: Her lines are no longer valid

parts.words: Her lines are no longer valid
parts.note: marriage lines, the certificate, have lost their force once the union is dissolved

explanation.definitionFit: A woman whose marriage has been legally ended holds a void wedding certificate.

clue.text: Courageous law-breaker in the beginning

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round

parts.note: start means beginning

indicators.note: breaker means the word law is broken up and its letters rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A brave criminal right at the start of his career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaker' turns LAW into WAL, which goes 'in' START.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart person is staunch and brave.

clue.text: Agony of fellows in the wrong?

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men are fellows

explanation.surface: Fellows who are wrong suffer agonies of guilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe suffering, physical or mental.

clue.text: Endless duffer at games needs a teacher

indicators.note: Endless means the final letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a rabbit is British slang for a poor player at cricket, tennis or golf

explanation.surface: A hopeless sportsman needs coaching.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'rabbit' is a weak player, especially a tail-end batsman in cricket; 'Endless' cuts off its T.
explanation.definitionFit: The title means master or teacher of Jewish law.

clue.text: Spa still overturning source of Archimedes' inspiration

parts.note: Bath is the English spa city

indicators.note: overturning means the word for still is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: but means still, as in 'but it moves'

explanation.surface: Water at a spa is said to inspire the Greek inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: Archimedes supposedly cried 'Eureka' on stepping into his bath; 'overturning' turns BUT into TUB.
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes had his displacement insight while stepping into a bath.

clue.text: Great fuss at university over right man in boat

parts.note: up means in residence at university
an oar is a rower, a crew member in a boat

explanation.surface: A row at Oxford over the choice of oarsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is a link; OAR for an oarsman is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy commotion or tumult.

clue.text: One trains climbers by distributing a log

parts.note: per means by, as in per post

indicators.note: distributing means spreading out the letters of 'a log' in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone coaches mountaineers by sharing out a logbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbers' tempts towards mountaineers, but these are climbing plants trained up a garden frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden arch or framework on which vines and roses are trained to grow.

clue.text: Scotch governor on the bottle?

parts.note: a pub device fixed to an upturned whisky bottle governs each measure poured

explanation.definitionFit: A British pub measuring device dispensing a fixed tot of spirit.

clue.text: Distinguished conductor appearing at Rome's order

indicators.note: order means the letters of 'at Rome's' are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A famous conductor turns up at the command of Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges AT ROMES, the apostrophe ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminent musician who leads an orchestra is given this honorific title.

clue.text: Round ends with green, that is obvious!

parts.note: O is round in shape
vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: A golf round finishes on the green, clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: VERT is green in heraldry; 'ends with' joins O to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means openly visible, not hidden.

clue.text: I castle in distress, but that is not yielding!

indicators.note: in distress means the letters of 'I castle in' are troubled into a new order

explanation.surface: A besieged castle declares it will not surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelastic means rigid, unable to stretch or give way.

clue.text: Mum has retired with the tiniest sum

parts.note: one cent, I for one, is the smallest sum of money

explanation.surface: Mother has retired on the smallest pension imaginable.
explanation.walkthrough: Mum means silent here, not mother; 'has' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep mum is to stay silent and say little.

clue.text: Some seed I blend to make it fit for the table

definitions.text: to make it fit for the table

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cook mixes a few seeds into a dish to make it suitable for serving.
explanation.definitionFit: Food fit to eat at a meal is safe to consume.
